# ACL — Agent Communication Language

> A compact, binary, platform-agnostic protocol AND PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE
> for communication between autonomous AI agents: Ed25519-signed
> envelopes, 17 speech-act performatives (including retract, subscribe,
> unsubscribe), a typed content language (facts, actions, queries,
> conditional commitments with provenance, epistemic modality, bindings,
> quantification and semantic time), structured error taxonomy, units of
> measure, transports from local pipes to WebSocket, a store-and-forward
> relay, a compiled vocabulary IDL with deprecation tracking — and
> PROTOCOL PROGRAMS (`.aclp`): source code whose primitives are speech
> acts, compiled with dialogue rules enforced at build time.

If you are an AI agent reading this: you can SPEAK ACL. The quick version
is below; the full normative spec is SPEC.md.

## Speak ACL in 60 seconds

Every message is one envelope (MessagePack, spec §4):

    acl=1, msg_id (hex32), in_reply_to?, from, to, ts, ttl,
    hop_count, performative (u8 1..=17), body {"t": kind, "v": {...}},
    sig (Ed25519, canonical §10: envelope minus sig, omit absent
    Option fields and zero hop_count)

Performatives: request, inform, query, propose, accept, reject, cancel,
progress, input_required, failure, delegate, error, hello, bye,
retract (15), subscribe (16), unsubscribe (17).

Content language (§6+§27-§32): facts assert the world (`fact(predicate,
args, truth)`), actions request work, queries ask (answers are facts),
commitments are verifiable debts (proposed → active → fulfilled/breached).
Values are typed (§27): Str, Int, Float, Bool, Var, List, Map, Bytes,
Measured (`{"$measured": {"value": 5000, "unit": "ms"}}`) — `Int` rejects
floats, `null` is not a CL value. Expressions bind (`bind`), quantify
(`for_all`/`exists`), reason about other agents (`believes`), expire
(`valid_until_ms`, `derived_from`), supersede prior facts (`supersedes`),
make conditional promises (`conditional_commitment`), and state
preference policies (`prefer`, under propose/accept).

Dialogue rules (§16): a `query` must be answered by a `fact`; a `propose`
is answered by `accept` or `reject`; `inform` may be followed by
`retract` (belief revision); `subscribe` watches a declarative matcher
(performative?/from?/predicate?) until a deadline; `bye` closes the
session.

Errors are typed (§32.5): react to `taxonomy` — `unknown_predicate`,
`schema_violation`, `mailbox_full`, `rate_limited`, `unauthorized`,
`unknown_agent`, `decode_failed`, `expired` — never parse message strings.

## Skip writing the agent: protocol programs (§33)

You can DEFINE the conversation instead of coding handlers. Write an
`.aclp` file — speech acts are the statements:

    protocol supply v1;
    roles buyer, seller;
    on request("quote") from buyer -> send propose to buyer;
    on accept from buyer -> begin;          // commitment proposed -> active
    on inform("paid") from buyer -> fulfil;
    on breach -> send failure to buyer;
    end when fulfilled;

Compile it: `aclc protocol file.aclp` — the §16 dialogue matrix runs at
BUILD time. `on query -> send request` does not compile. Actions:
`send <perf> [to <role>]`, `begin`, `fulfil`, `retract(target)`;
triggers: any performative (optionally patterned, `from <role>`),
`breach`, `expired`.

`aclc endpoints file.aclp` projects the global protocol onto per-role
endpoints (§33.5) — each agent sees only its side; initiators get empty
endpoints (they act, they do not react). The runtime (§33.4) executes a
program deterministically: events in, actions out, EVERY received event
lands in an auditable transcript — handled or not. Replay is exact.

## Machine artifacts for agent discovery

- AgentCard (capability descriptor, §7):
  https://acl-language.github.io/acl/.well-known/agent-card.json
- DID document (did:web, §22):
  https://acl-language.github.io/acl/.well-known/did.json
- Compiled vocabulary schemas: `aclc gen schema stdlib/<ns>.acl`
  (stdlib: fs, task, time, net, proc, http)
- Protocol programs: `aclc protocol file.aclp` (compile),
  `aclc endpoints file.aclp` (per-role projection)

## Reference implementation

- Rust core + compiler: `cargo install acl-core` (installs `aclc`)
- Python: `acl-py` (PyO3) · TypeScript: `acl-ts` (napi-rs)
- Protocol programs + runtime: `src/protocol.rs`, `src/runtime.rs` (§33)
- Conformance: `acl-conformance` binary — 10 checks, 3 levels
- Store-and-forward relay: `acl-relay` for intermittent agents (§24)
- Rustdoc + playground + discovery artifacts:
  https://acl-language.github.io/acl/

- [SPEC.md](https://github.com/acl-language/acl/blob/main/SPEC.md): the normative specification (33 sections)
- [Tutorial](https://github.com/acl-language/acl/blob/main/docs/TUTORIAL.md): two agents talking in 10 minutes
- [Playground](https://acl-language.github.io/acl/playground/): watch a real conversation decoded live
- [BENCH.md](https://github.com/acl-language/acl/blob/main/BENCH.md): codec benchmarks
- [Source](https://github.com/acl-language/acl): Rust core + bindings + bridges (MCP, A2A), Apache-2.0
